subject: Island 014 Royal Palace unified volumetric cathedral gable facade blockout

inputs.evidenceIntegrity: All v003 000/045/315/close SVG and JPEG evidence listed by capture-manifest.v3.json was reviewed; the JPEGs are browser rasterizations of the immutable actual-mesh SVG captures.

familyDifferenceAssessment.finding: The retired applied frame/rail grammar is replaced by a closed central gable and two closed occupied wing/pylon volumes. The new family nevertheless introduces a different representation-level failure: an oversized flat-wing skin with standalone projected openings.

perViewScores.note: All four bays can be counted frontally, and door/rose order is obvious. The two enormous planar wings dominate the facade, the pointed door arch/recess is hidden behind a blank central slab, and the rose remains a separate thick disk rather than an embedded opening.

The near wing reads as a giant flat card with standalone projected bay boxes. The rose stands far proud of the gable, the door loses its arch/recess hierarchy, and the far/upper bays are not reliably countable.
The opposite source-adjacent view confirms the same oversized wing card, forward rose disk, blank door slab, and loss of four-bay countability.

The close view shows the central door surface as an uninterrupted faceted slab; the required dark recess, multi-layer masonry arch, royal bee focal detail, and occupied vertical connection are not readable.

doorFirstFocalPoint.finding: Door scale makes it first, but it is a blank slab rather than the required recessed royal doorway.

roseEmbeddedNotProud.finding: Both obliques show a thick rose disk and reveal assembly standing visibly forward of the gable.

fourBaysCountableAt045.finding: Only the near bays are immediately legible; far/upper openings collapse behind the central and wing masses.

fourBaysCountableAt315.finding: The mirrored view likewise loses reliable four-bay countability.

unifiedSkinWithinAcceptedSilhouette.finding: The large planar wings extend and dominate beyond the accepted palace front read, materially changing apparent width and hierarchy.

standaloneBayBoxesAbsent.finding: Oblique views show thick independent reveal boxes projecting from the wing faces.

longFloatingRailsAbsent.finding: The retired long-rail construction is absent.

bannerObstructionAbsent.finding: No banner blocks the door or stairs in the supplied evidence.

zFightingOrOpenGapAbsent.finding: No z-fighting or open-backed gap is visibly proven by the supplied materials-off captures.

defects.finding: The supposedly occupied pylons are broad planar cards that dominate and alter the accepted palace silhouette.
The rose remains a standalone thick disk, directly violating the new family's defining embed hypothesis.
All four occupied bays are not individually countable in either 45-degree or 315-degree evidence.
The giant central panel hides the required recessed door/arch hierarchy and erases source-specific royal detail.

largestMismatch: The source facade is a compact, deeply occupied vertical cathedral axis nested inside the palace. This blockout instead places a blank central door slab, a proud rose disk, and four applied boxes across two giant planar wings, producing a broad civic mask rather than integrated honey-cathedral architecture.

correctionDisposition.reason: The defects are not one bounded parameter hypothesis: fixing them requires replacing wing proportions/topology, rebuilding the door/arch volume, embedding the rose, and re-laying all four openings. That is a new representation family, not one measurable correction.

terminalReason: Every required category is below 0.85; worst score is 0.38. Strict rejects for a proud rose, standalone bay boxes, fewer than four countable bays at both obliques, and accepted-silhouette change are present. The family is not viable for one bounded correction.
